sanskrit: तस्मान्नार्हा वयं हन्तुं धार्तराष्ट्रान्स्वबान्धवान् । स्वजनं हि कथं हत्वा सुखिनः स्याम माधव ॥
hindiTranslation: इसलिये अपने बान्धव इन धृतराष्ट्रसम्बन्धियों को मारने के लिये हम योग्य नहीं हैं क्योंकि हे माधव अपने कुटुम्बियों को मारकर हम कैसे सुखी होंगे ॥
englishTranslation: Therefore, we are not fit to kill our own kinsmen, the sons of Dhritarashtra. How could we be happy after killing our relatives, O Madhava?
speaker: Arjuna
simpleMeaning: Arjuna says the Kaurava side are his own relatives, so killing them would not bring happiness.
simpleInsight: You can feel the cost of violence before you act, and that honesty matters.
detailedMeaning: Arjuna looks at the men he is meant to fight and sees family where he expected enemies. Krishna is pressing him toward action, but Arjuna's heart is breaking under the thought of killing his own kin.
modernRelevance: A player who wins a match by injuring his close friend gets the medal and loses the friend. Arjuna puts the same question to Madhava: how could anyone be happy after killing their own relatives?
translationLiteral: तस्मात् (therefore) / न अर्हाः (not fit) / वयम् (we) / हन्तुम् (to kill) / धार्तराष्ट्रान् (the sons of Dhritarashtra) / स्व-बान्धवान् (our own relatives) / स्व-जनम् (our own people) / हि (indeed) / कथम् (how) / हत्वा (having killed) / सुखिनः (happy) / स्याम (we would be) / माधव (O Madhava)
insight: Arjuna concludes that he and his brothers are unfit to kill their kinsmen, because no happiness could follow.
